events.description:
Flagship placement-simulation event replicating the actual internship and placement interview process for CE students, assessing and sharpening their technical and behavioural interview skills. Participation is mandatory for CE students who wish to compete in other Nirmaan events.

Round 1: Online assessment
Round 2: GD
Round 3: Personal Interview
rules: Individual participation only.
Eligibility: 1st, 2nd and 3rd year CE students only.
Students must appear in both rounds to qualify and receive certification.
Any misconduct or malpractice during interviews leads to disqualification.
Panel evaluation is final and binding.

events.description:
A premier civil engineering design challenge that brings together architectural innovation, AutoCAD proficiency, and practical engineering expertise. Participants transform visionary academic building concepts into technical designs while demonstrating their problem-solving abilities through real-world construction challenges.

Round 1: Basic AutoCAD skill test.
Round 2: Design your dream academic building.
Round 3: Interpret drawings, detect errors, and solve simulated site problems.
rules: Open to students from all branches.
Team size: 3–4 members.
No inter-year teams allowed.
At least two Civil Engineering students are compulsory in every team.
Participants must complete all AutoCAD design tasks and the final site-engineering challenge within the prescribed time. Judges’ decisions will be final.
Average CPI of team must be below 8.

events.description:
A sustainable concrete design challenge in which participants develop and test pervious concrete, a specially designed concrete that allows water to pass through its interconnected voids. The event challenges teams to design an effective mix, cast specimens, and evaluate their water permeability, structural strength, and physical integrity to achieve the best balance between drainage performance and durability.

Round 1: Knowledge Test
Round 2: Abstract Submission (Mix Design) [Elimination]
Round 3: Casting, Laboratory Testing + Questionnaire
rules: Only Civil Engineering students from 2nd and 3rd year are eligible.
Team size: 3 members per team.
Inter-year teams are allowed.
Teams must follow the approved mix design and use only materials provided or permitted by the organizers.
Evaluation will be based on mix design, water permeability, specimen integrity, and compressive strength, subject to laboratory feasibility. Judges’ decisions will be final.
Average CPI of team must be below 8.

events.description:
Linkidge – Bridge Making Competition

Linkidge is a structural engineering challenge in which participants design, construct, and test a bridge made using ice-cream popsicle sticks. The competition encourages students to apply the fundamental principles of structural analysis, load distribution, stability, and material efficiency to create a lightweight yet strong bridge. Teams must develop an effective bridge design that can withstand the maximum possible load before structural failure. The winning team will be the one whose bridge achieves the highest load-bearing capacity while complying with the specified construction rules and dimensions.

Round 1: Bridge Design Abstract Submission [Elimination]
Round 2: Bridge Construction, Load Testing + Technical Questionnaire.
rules: Each team must consist of 3–4 members, including at least 2 Civil Engineering students.
No inter-year teams are allowed; all team members must belong to the same academic year.
Bridges must be constructed using ice-cream popsicle sticks and only the adhesives or other materials permitted by the organizers.
All bridges must comply with the specified dimensions, construction guidelines, and submission deadlines.
Bridges will be evaluated based on maximum load-bearing capacity, structural stability, construction quality, and material efficiency.
Any bridge violating the prescribed rules or dimensions may be disqualified.
The judges’ decision will be final.
Average CPI of team must be below 8.

events.description:
Codigo is a proposed coding competition aimed at enhancing students’ programming skills, logical reasoning, and problem-solving abilities. The event will provide a platform for students to demonstrate their technical proficiency and encourage greater participation in coding-related activities.

Round 1 – Online Test: Participants attempt questions covering CS fundamentals, aptitude, OOP, DBMS, and SQL.
Round 2 – Coding Round: Participants solve programming problems within the prescribed time. This is an elimination round.
Round 3 – Mock Interviews: Shortlisted participants undergo mock interviews focused on technical knowledge and campus placements.
rules: Individual participation only.
Eligibility: 1st, 2nd and 3rd year CE students only.

events.description:
StrataGem is an academic case study and problem-solving competition designed to challenge students to think critically, develop innovative solutions, and defend their ideas before a panel of experts.

Round 1: The Case Brief
Teams will receive a faculty-approved problem statement and submit a two-page executive summary outlining their problem analysis, proposed solution, key findings, and recommendations via Google Forms. The submissions will be evaluated, and 10–15 teams will be shortlisted for Round 2.
Round 2: The Expert Courtroom
Shortlisted teams will prepare a 7–8 slide presentation outlining their analysis, proposed solution, implementation strategy, and expected deliverables. They will present on the main stage before a panel of professors, who will evaluate their approach, feasibility, and ability to defend and optimise their solutions.
rules: Teams must consist of 2–3 members, with at least one Civil Engineering student in each team.
Students from different academic years and branches may participate, provided the team meets the eligibility criteria.
Round 1 submissions must be limited to a two-page summary of the assigned problem statement.
Shortlisted teams will prepare a presentation of 7–8 slides for Round 2.
Teams must present their analysis, proposed solution, implementation strategy, and expected deliverables.
Presentations will be followed by questions from the panel of professors.
The use of AI tools is strictly prohibited for preparing summaries, presentations, or other competition submissions.
All submissions and presentations must be original, with sources appropriately acknowledged.
The organising committee may disqualify teams for plagiarism, AI use, rule violations, or failure to meet submission requirements.

events.description:
Bounding Box is a multi-round, team-based technical event that challenges participants to solve real-world civil engineering problems using data analysis and fundamental machine learning techniques. Participants will explore datasets, identify meaningful patterns, engineer relevant features, and develop ML models to generate practical, data-driven solutions for civil engineering challenges.

Round 1: Brainstorm — Problem Ideation & Abstract Submission
In this round, participants will identify a civil engineering problem and propose a data-driven approach to address it using basic machine learning techniques. Teams must prepare a 4–5 page abstract.
Round 2: Byte — Model Development & Technical Evaluation (Elimination)
Participants must be ready to present their project files, executable code, and GitHub repository. This is an elimination round, and teams will advance based on the quality of their implementation, model evaluation, and understanding of the problem.
Round 3: Boardroom — Technical Interview & Final Evaluation (Elimination)
The final round consists of one-on-one technical interviews with the shortlisted finalists.
rules: Open to students from all branches.
Team size: 2–4 members.
No inter-year teams allowed.
At least one Civil Engineering student is compulsory in every team.

events.description:
Survivor Series – The Ultimate Test of Survival

Survivor Series is an exhilarating, multi-round team competition designed to test participants’ knowledge, creativity, memory, teamwork, and ability to perform under pressure.

Round 1: The Ultimate Quiz & Audio-Visual Challenge (Elimination)
Teams compete in a two-part challenge comprising a pen-and-paper quiz and an audio-visual round featuring memes, iconic dialogues, songs, images, and mystery clips. Scores from both parts are combined, and the top 10 teams advance to the next round.
Round 2: Head-to-Head Showdown + Death Round (Elimination)
The 10 qualifying teams face off in five head-to-head matchups in a movie-themed Dumb Charades challenge. The five winning teams qualify directly, while the five losing teams enter the Death Round, featuring logic puzzles, memory tests, and rapid-fire pressure challenges. Only one team survives this final battle to claim the sixth finalist spot.
Round 3: The Classified Challenge (Final Round)
The six finalist teams face a secret challenge that will test their teamwork, strategic thinking, and ability to adapt under pressure. The details remain classified until the round begins. Only one team can emerge as the ultimate Survivor Series champion.
rules: Combined event for all branches.
Team size: 3 members, with at least one Civil Engineering student.
No cross-year teams.
